cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the believers in Colossae (Colossians 1:1-2). He's just spent a big stretch lifting up Christ (Colossians 1:15-20). Now Paul turns to himself and his sufferings for them.

cards.question: Paul is suffering for the believers in Colossae. How does he say he feels about it?

answers.text: He is worn out by it

cards.text: Friend, I grumble when the oven timer beeps too loud, and Paul's out here REJOICING in suffering. Then he says, "I fill up in my flesh what is lacking in regard to Christ’s afflictions," and he says who it's for.

cards.question: Paul says he suffers for the sake of Christ’s ___, which is the church.

cards.text: Paul says he became the church's servant. He got the job by a commission, so somebody handed it to him.

cards.question: Paul became the church's servant by a commission. Who gave it to him?

cards.text: God handing out jobs? Friend, I KNOW that one: one night I'm a worn-out stamper in a junk drawer, the next I'm running a whole bakery. And Paul tells them exactly what his job is for.

cards.question: God gave Paul a commission as the church's servant. What is it for?

answers.text: To fully proclaim the word of God
To set up elders in every town

cards.text: Paul calls the word of God a mystery, hidden for ages and generations. Friend, I did years in a junk drawer and thought THAT was forever.

cards.question: Paul says the mystery is still hidden, even from God's saints.

cards.text: Now God makes a choice. He makes known the glorious riches of this mystery, and Paul says among whom.

cards.question: God chose to make known the glorious riches of the mystery. Among whom?
So what is this mystery, hidden for ages and now made known?

answers.text: Christ in you the hope of glory
The law within you the lamp of truth
A kingdom restored to the sons of Israel

cards.text: Christ in you, the hope of glory. Paul says, "We proclaim Him, admonishing and teaching everyone with all wisdom," and then he tells them the goal.

cards.question: Paul proclaims Christ and teaches everyone with all wisdom. What is the goal?

answers.text: To present everyone perfect in Christ
To make everyone teachers of the law
To bring everyone under the law of Moses

cards.text: To that end Paul labors, striving with all His energy working powerfully within him. Friend, if I ran this bakery on MY energy, the ovens would shut off by noon and you'd find me asleep in the flour bin.
Paul's still writing to the believers in Colossae. He wants them to know how hard he's struggling for them, and not only for them.

cards.question: Paul is struggling for the believers in Colossae. Who else is he struggling for?

answers.text: Those at Laodicea and all who have not met him
The believers in Jerusalem and all of Judea
The church at Corinth and the saints in Achaia

cards.text: Struggling hard for people he's never even met face to face. And here's what he wants for them: hearts that are encouraged, and people knit together by something.

cards.question: Paul wants their hearts encouraged and wants them knit together in ___.

cards.text: He wants them filled with the full riches of complete understanding, so they know the mystery of God, namely Christ. And in Christ, Paul says, the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.

cards.question: How many of the treasures of wisdom and knowledge does Paul say are hidden in Christ?

cards.text: ALL of them, friend, not most and not a bunch: ALL. Then Paul tells them why he's saying all this.

cards.question: Why does Paul tell the Colossians all this about Christ?

answers.text: So no one deceives them with smooth talk
So they will send him a gift
So they will come and visit him

cards.text: Smooth rhetoric, friend, like that phone call saying you won a cruise you never even entered. Then Paul talks about how close he is to them.

cards.question: Paul is with the Colossian believers in body as he writes.
Paul is absent in body but present with them in spirit. What does he delight to see in them?

answers.text: Their orderly condition and firm faith in Christ
Their growing crowds and new meeting places
Their generous gifts to the poor in Jerusalem
